{{Short description|British mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
{{other people|Nicholas Young}}
'''Nicholas John Young''' is a British [[mathematician]] working in [[operator theory]],  [[functional analysis]] and [[complex analysis|several complex variables]]. He is a [[research professor]] at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk/stafflist|title=Faculty of Mathematics and Physical Sciences - Staff list|website=University of Leeds}}</ref> Much of his work has been about the interaction of operator theory and [[Complex analysis|function theory]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Axler |first1=Sheldon|authorlink=Sheldon Axler |title=Holomorphic Spaces |date=1998 |publisher=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute Publications |isbn=978-0-521-63193-8}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Young has written more than a hundred papers,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www1.maths.leeds.ac.uk/~nicholas/publist.pdf|title=Publications of Nicholas Young|date=17 March 2018|website=University of Leeds|access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref> over 30  of them in collaboration with [[Jim Agler]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet|title=Search Publications database|website=Americal Mathematical Society|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref><ref>[https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet MathSciNet]</ref> He is the author of the book ''An Introduction to [[Hilbert Space]]''.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_igwFHKwcyYC|title=An Introduction to Hilbert Space|last=Young|first=N.|date=1988-07-21|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521337175|language=en}}</ref>

His Ph.D. adviser was [[Vlastimil Pták]], and he has had 5 Ph.D. students.<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=208641 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>
